title: AVL9 promotes colorectal carcinoma cell migration via regulating EGFR expression
author: Wu, Chen, et al.
materials: The tissue microarray construction (TMA, #HStmA150CS02) containing 83 human CRC cancer specimens and 83 non-cancer specimens was bought from Shanghai Outdo Biotech, Shanghai, China and analyzed by two pathologists in a blinded manner. Detailed clinical information is included, for example, gender, age, tumor size, differentiation, T classification, N status, M status and stages. An anti-AVL9 antibody (ab175108; Abcam, Cambridge, MA, USA) at a dilution of 1:500 was used to detect the expression of AVL9. The classification of ICH staining (immunohistochemical staining) results was as mentioned [35]. The study was approved by the ethics committee of Shanghai East Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine.

The expression of AVL9 in CRC cells were downregulated by transient with two different siRNAs which were synthesized by GenePharma, Shanghai, China. siRNA sense sequences were as follows: siNC (sense 5-UUCUCCGAACGUGUCACGU-dTdT-3), siAVL9-1 (sense 5-GCCACAGUAUUUGGUAUCUdTdT-3), siAVL9-2 (sense 5-GGACUCUUCAUGGCAUCAAdTdT-3). Overexpressed plasmid, a full-length AVL9 cDNA was cloned into pcDNA 3.1 mammalian expression vector, was purchased from Vigene Biosciences, Shandong, China. Following the manufacturer’s instructions, siRNAs or plasmids were transfected using lipofectamine 3000 (Invitrogen, Thermo Fisher Scientific, US). In order to stably overexpressed or knockdown the expression of AVL9, Lentiviral particles (Lv6-AVL9 and Lv6-NC; Lv3-shAVL9 and Lv3-shNC based on siAVL9-1 and siNC sequence) was purchased from Gene Pharma, Shanghai, China. CRC cells stably infected cells were selected by puromycin (2μg/ml) after transducing cells with lentiviral particles.

steps.title: Prepare tissue microarray
steps.instruction: Obtain the tissue microarray (TMA, #HStmA150CS02) containing 83 human colorectal cancer specimens and 83 non‑cancer specimens from Shanghai Outdo Biotech, Shanghai, China.

steps.title: Perform immunohistochemical staining
steps.instruction: Stain the TMA sections with anti‑AVL9 antibody (ab175108, Abcam) diluted 1:500 to detect AVL9 expression.

steps.title: Blindly evaluate IHC results
steps.instruction: Have two pathologists independently assess the immunohistochemical staining results in a blinded manner, classifying the staining according to the method described in reference [35].

steps.title: Synthesize AVL9 siRNAs
steps.instruction: Order the following siRNA oligonucleotides from GenePharma, Shanghai, China:

steps.title: Transient siRNA transfection
steps.instruction: Transfect colorectal cancer cells with each siRNA using Lipofectamine 3000 (Invitrogen, Thermo Fisher Scientific, US) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Transient plasmid transfection
steps.instruction: Transfect cells with the full‑length AVL9 cDNA cloned into the pcDNA 3.1 vector (purchased from Vigene Biosciences, Shandong, China) using Lipofectamine 3000 as per the supplier’s instructions.

steps.title: Generate stable AVL9 lines
steps.instruction: Infect CRC cells with lentiviral particles (Lv6‑AVL9, Lv6‑NC; Lv3‑shAVL9, Lv3‑shNC based on siAVL9‑1 and siNC sequences) purchased from GenePharma, Shanghai, China, then select stably transduced cells with puromycin at 2 µg/ml.

steps.title: Obtain public CRC expression data
steps.instruction: Download mRNA expression data for tumor and matched non‑tumor colorectal cancer tissues from the GEPIA online tool (http://gepia.cancer-pku.cn/) using the TCGA database.

steps.title: Run GSEA analysis
steps.instruction: Perform Gene Set Enrichment Analysis with GSEA version 4.0.3 (https://www.gsea‑msigdb.org/gsea/index.jsp) to compare AVL9‑high versus AVL9‑low expression groups.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of results
steps.instruction: Analyze data from three independent experiments using GraphPad Prism 8; present values as mean ± SD; compare groups with Student’s t‑test or one‑way ANOVA; assess associations with χ² test; consider p < 0.05 statistically significant.
